title: Design Systems
description: Build reusable component libraries and design tokens. Tests component specification, token architecture, and library auditing.

seo.overviewBody: Design systems ensure visual consistency and development speed across multi-product teams. Senior product designers evaluate candidates on defining design tokens (colors, typography, spacing, shadows), applying Atomic Design principles, and building reusable Figma component libraries.

deliverables.title: 1. Figma Design System Library File
deliverables.desc: Figma UI library containing design tokens, auto-layout components, auto-updating typography styles, and dark mode variants.

deliverables.title: 2. Design Token & Component Guidelines Document
deliverables.desc: Documentation detailing component usage guidelines, accessibility rules, and spatial grid standards.

deliverables.title: 3. Component State & Variant Specification
deliverables.desc: Component library spec illustrating default, hover, focus, active, disabled, and loading states.

faqs.question: What is the Atomic Design methodology?
faqs.answer: Atomic Design organizes UI interfaces into 5 distinct levels: Atoms (basic tags/buttons), Molecules (search bars), Organisms (headers), Templates (layouts), and Pages (final UI screens).

faqs.question: What are design tokens in a design system?
faqs.answer: Design tokens are named sub-atomic values (e.g. color-primary-500: #0066CC, spacing-md: 16px) that store visual design decisions in code-ready formats.

faqs.question: How do component variants streamline design in Figma?
faqs.answer: Variants combine related component states (e.g. primary button vs disabled button) into a single master component container with customizable properties.
